title: The Anomalon Boundary: Primitive Difference, Structure, and the Authority Boundary of Meaning
description: This paper establishes the root authority boundary of finite verification in its most cautious form: every authoritative claim must descend to Primitive Difference, Structure, or a typed refusal. We formalize the Anomalon not as a metaphysical beginning or cosmology, but strictly as a recursion and restart boundary: the boundary object produced when a finite authority system exhausts all admitted repairs and retains a typed obstruction. An Anomalon permits only three lawful continuations: typed refusal, lift request with a preservation witness, or next-iteration restart seed. We establish the Surviving Primitive Difference trichotomy: exact discrepancies vanish as gauge (quotient residual [h] = 0 in H^1), unclosed discrepancies represent active closure failure (Gamma_2 > 0), and closed non-exact discrepancies survive as stable structure ([h] != 0 in H^1, Gamma_2 = 0). Furthermore, we formalize the Minimal Knowable System (MKS) as a ten-role proposed interface specification for systems to be terminalizable under this calculus. This monograph assigns no authorization and changes no jurisdiction. It carries no operational authority or institutional standing.
